name: generate_study_site
description: Scaffold a static study site from one course config. This file is the contract. The implementation an agent runs is node kit/scaffold.mjs. There is no server here. Pass the config fields as the arguments. Required: siteTitle, course, throughline, textbook, maps, threads, stations. throughline is one idea, in one or two sentences. The home picture makes it true and one drag makes the sentence false. The learner reads the lede and that picture, not the config. Do not call when textbook.title is missing, TODO, or a placeholder: ask for the title, authors, edition, and a URL or chapter list first, unless the task already told you to pick a free book, in which case cite the page you read and set confidence below 1. Each station needs summary, observe, and source with chapter and section. observe is the instruction under the picture and may stay put. The sentence that is false in another state is viz.claim (whenTrue and whenFalse), not observe. A flashcard needs front, back, source, and station, the stop it drills. A problem needs hint, answer { tex, text, values }, station, and source.exercise. A concept needs station and the same section as that station. visualization is "two-addresses" (a complex point; it talks about Arg and the seam), "number-line" (one real number, up to 3 preset chips), "graph" (drag x, purple output; fn is poly, abs, or arg), or "shape" (one 2x2 on a square: action rotate, stretch, stretch-x, or shear, or sample matrices). stretch is uniform and stays a square; stretch-x is [[t,0],[0,1]] and is a square only at t=1; rotate stays a square, so use claim test near; shear flips image-square; a reflection is still a square, so use det-positive. The readout says square or not a square, plus det and the marked corner. Home viz.picture may be shape (the square, no chips) when the throughline is a matrix. Any other picture is kind "custom" and module "./stations/<id>.js", a file already stamped beside the config. This call copies that file and does not draw it. A missing file is an error. A file that still exports STAMP_OPEN is unfinished, same as kind "reading", which is an unfinished placeholder, not a finished stop. colourKeys text is this course's words for the tokens cart, polar, input, and output. Do not copy Cartesian or Arg onto a course that is not about them. Config loop is camelCase: reframeRounds and reframers. Do not put reframe_rounds inside the config. This call writes the folder and copies any stations/<id>.js from beside the config. It does not draw custom pictures, recompute answers, or run reviewers. Do not start a reframe round while unfinished stops are still listed. After the folder exists, build in batches of 2 to 4 rounds, then close, then mid, then wide, then at most 3 reframe rounds of 3 independent reframers, one rebuttal each, and a council. Reviewers decide. They do not ask the user. The only ask is a textbook you cannot find a page for. If the task names the course and tells you to pick a free book, cite the page you read. Set confidence below 1 when the licence is not on that page. Do not ask, and do not invent a section number. A batch is 2 to 4 pictured stations. Do not add a reading row to cover the next section. The example config is a finished pictured slice, not a syllabus to copy. kit/examples/linear-algebra.config.json is the other course. Every generated picture uses js/core/anim.js. createFrame is the one paint frame. createMotion is the play clock. stop and cancel drop a queued callback, on unmount and on pause. Steps use elapsed time. A hidden tab pauses the clock and does not jump the picture when it returns. The control that starts a motion says Pause while it runs. A second click freezes the picture where it is. It does not jump to the end. prefers-reduced-motion steps instead of playing, and that step button does not say Pause. A drag may show one coarse frame. The status stays on that finished picture until the next finished picture replaces it. Pause and idle draw the full final, and that bitmap matches the canvas backing store up to a long edge of 1400 and a device pixel ratio cap of 3. The canvas is resized only when that size changes. Chips, keys, and pointer-up paint immediately. Pointer-move paints once per frame. A later click continues that motion from the frozen value. When the motion has finished, a later click plays it again from the start. The picture does not jump backward. A film waits for each sharp frame and does not skip it. It does not precompute every sharp frame. The playing frame and the still share the long-edge cap of 1400. When the bitmap already on screen is that final, the page does not paint it again. A camera spin may use the 3D view's frame. That frame pauses while the tab is hidden, and a gap longer than a frame does not move the camera. The button says Pause. A second click freezes the angle, and a later click continues it. The view may draw under device pixel ratio 3 so a large picture stays inside its pixel budget. That budget is the cap. A station may carry one film: a HyperFrames page in films/ beside the config, made and QA'd with the manim-hyperframes-matrix MCP (bundle_page with controls false and qa true; ship only qa_clean). The page has one paused timeline on window.__tl, beats in window.__beats, readouts marked data-readout, and no controls, ticker, or timers. This call copies films/ and writes the film list. The station's film panel is the play button and follows the same clock rules: Pause freezes, a later click continues, a finished film plays again, a hidden tab moves nothing, nothing is drawn while paused, and reduced motion steps between beats. Under 835px the page stacks the plane above the staircase or the readouts, at 15px or more, and does not scroll sideways. Landscape scale starts at 835px so the 23px cite stays at 15px. A citation whose PDF number was not checked says so and does not invent one. A film cites chapter, section, and the equation, example, or exercise it shows. A film whose page is missing is an error.

loop.reviewer_order: after the builder: close, then mid, then wide
loop.council: picks one pitch or a synthesis and writes the reason; the next builder batch prototypes it; close, mid, and wide run before another reframe
loop.citations: chapter and section on every station, concept, and card; chapter, section, and exercise on every problem
loop.ask_user_only_when: you cannot find a textbook the task did not tell you to choose
loop.films: made with the manim-hyperframes-matrix MCP; bundle_page qa must be clean; the close reviewer checks a film's motion and its readout on a phone

siteTitle.description: The name in the header and the browser tab.

course.description: Course code or name, such as MAT 412.

description.description: One sentence for the meta description.

throughline.description: The one idea the whole site teaches, across every test and map.

storagePrefix.description: localStorage prefix. Default study:. Do not reuse another site's prefix on the same origin.

ledeByMap.description: Home-page sentence per map. Each map gets its own lede. The throughline still governs every page.

title.description: The course textbook, or the course handout when that is the actual text. Empty, TODO, or a placeholder is invalid. The scaffold exits 2 and the agent asks.

url.description: Primary link. Use the HTML edition when both exist.

confidence.description: 1 when the user named the book. Below 1, note must say what is still uncertain. A missing title still means stop and ask.

loop.description: CamelCase caps in the config. The top-level loop object on this file is the same procedure in snake_case. Do not put reframe_rounds in the config.

reframeRounds.description: Cap on zoom-out rounds. Stop earlier when pitches converge.

reframers.description: Independent reframer agents per zoom-out round.

chapter.description: Textbook chapter. Use 0 only when the idea is outside the numbered chapters, and say so in note.

exercise.description: Required on problems. The handout's number when it is not a confirmed book exercise, and then say so in note.

url.description: Section URL. The source tag links here when it is set.

tex.description: Prose the learner reads, with $...$ around TeX.

text.description: The same answer in plain text. No $ and no TeX commands.

values.description: Named numbers a test recomputes. {} only when the answer has no number.

kind.description: reading is an unfinished placeholder. A finished teaching stop is viz or custom. Exactly one station is map. flashcards is the one-card deck. practice is the question list.

visualization.description: Built-in pictures. two-addresses is one complex point. number-line is one real number. graph drags x and draws the output in purple. shape applies one 2x2 to a square. Any other picture is a custom station. Do not fake it.

module.description: Only for kind custom. Must be ./stations/<id>.js, the same id as the station. The file lives beside the config and is copied in.

map.description: A map id, or shared for a stop that sits on every map.

observe.description: The instruction under the picture. It may stay put. The sentence that flips is viz.claim, not this field.

tie.description: Optional sentence that places the stop on the map. The shell writes one if this is empty.

viz.description: Start value and sentence for a built-in picture. Preset chips are controls. At most 3.

picture.description: Home only. point is one complex dot. line is one real dot. shape is the square with no chips. Omit it and the home picks point when the site has two-addresses, shape when the only pictures are shape, otherwise line.

fn.description: graph only. poly uses coefficients. abs is |x|. arg is the principal angle of the angle you walked, which jumps. No eval.

poly.description: graph coefficients, constant term first. y = c0 + c1 x + c2 x^2 + ...

action.description: shape only. stretch is the same factor on both axes. stretch-x scales only x, [[t, 0], [0, 1]]. rotate stays a square at every angle. shear is a square only at t = 0. Do not set this and samples together.

samples.description: shape only. Matrices blended by t. Do not set this and action together.

claim.description: The sentence that is true in one state and false in another. This is not observe. A graph uses op. A shape uses test: image-square, near, or det-positive.

station.description: The station id that carries the film. One film per station.

src.description: A page beside the config, copied with films/shared/.

lede.description: One or two sentences: the move the film shows, with the numbers it uses.

source.description: Chapter and section, plus the equation, example, or exercise in note or exercise. The section matches the station.
